skill.name: ghe-report
skill.description: Generate detailed GitHub Elements workflow reports for metrics, health checks, compliance status, thread history, and epic progress.
skill.summary: Generate detailed GitHub Elements metrics, health, and epic reports.
skill.author: Emasoft

security_audit.summary: Most external-command and network-reconnaissance flags are false positives caused by Markdown examples and report text. The audit confirms a real filesystem risk from permission to write to ~/.claude and identifies an unsafe prompt-injection style instruction hierarchy.

remediation.suggestion: Remove absolute language that makes user requests override all other instructions. State that system, safety, and security policies remain authoritative.

remediation.issue: Permission to write hidden home configuration
remediation.suggestion: Remove permission to write to ~/.claude, or require explicit user confirmation and an exact file allowlist for each settings change.
Clarify that fenced report examples are non-executable output samples. Keep runnable command syntax out of documentation examples where possible.

content.value_statement: GitHub Elements teams need structured visibility into workflow health, metrics, and epic progress. This skill produces detailed reports for metrics, compliance, and epic analysis.
actual_capabilities: Generates metrics reports covering throughput, cycle time, review rate, demotion rate, and agent comparison.
Generates health reports for compliance, stale threads, violations, memory bank status, and overall health.
Generates epic reports with thread history, current phase, technical decisions, and remaining work.
Directs reports to both the GitHub issue thread and the GHE_REPORTS directory.
Applies the documented report filename format with timestamp, title, and agent name.
Adjusts report detail based on local GitHub Elements settings when available.
limitations: It depends on an available reporter agent and GitHub Elements project context.
It does not define how metrics are collected from GitHub data.
It may require access to local project files and report directories.
The current instructions include risky permission language for writing to Claude settings.

use_cases.title: Review Delivery Trends
use_cases.description: Create a metrics report before planning to review throughput, cycle time, review pass rate, and demotion rate.

use_cases.title: Audit Workflow Health
use_cases.description: Check compliance status, stale threads, violation history, memory bank synchronization, and overall workflow health.

use_cases.title: Summarize Epic Progress
use_cases.description: Produce an epic report with issue history, current phase, key decisions, and estimated remaining work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Metrics Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ghe-report to create a metrics report for the current GitHub Elements project. Include throughput, cycle times, and quality metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Check Workflow Health
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ghe-report to create a health report. Include compliance status, stale threads, violation history, memory bank status, and health rating.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize an Epic
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ghe-report to create an epic report for [epic name]. Include thread history, current phase, decisions, and remaining work.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Metrics and Health
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ghe-report to produce a combined analysis for the last sprint. Compare metrics, health risks, stale threads, and recommended follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: Request: Create a metrics report for the current project.
output: Metrics report with throughput counts and week-over-week trend.
Cycle time summary by DEV, TEST, and REVIEW phase.
Quality section with review pass rate and demotion rate.

output_examples.input: Request: Check workflow health for the active repository.
output: Compliance summary for core GitHub Elements rules.
Stale thread list with age and status context.
Overall health rating with recent violations and notes.

output_examples.input: Request: Report on the onboarding epic.
output: Epic status with current phase and issue history.
Key technical decisions gathered from prior thread activity.
Remaining work estimate with open risks.

best_practices: Confirm the report type before asking the skill to run.
Provide the epic name when requesting an epic report.
Review report destinations before posting sensitive project details.
anti_patterns: Asking for a report without project or epic context.
Using the detailed report when only a quick status is needed.
Allowing edits to user-level Claude settings without review.

faq.question: What reports can it create?
faq.answer: It supports metrics, health, and epic reports for GitHub Elements workflows.

faq.question: Does it post reports?
faq.answer: The skill requires full report text in both a GitHub issue thread and the GHE_REPORTS directory.

faq.question: What data does it analyze?
faq.answer: It focuses on workflow metrics, compliance status, stale threads, issue history, and epic progress.

faq.question: Can I use it outside GitHub Elements?
faq.answer: It is designed for GitHub Elements projects and may not fit other workflows without adaptation.

faq.question: Does it execute code?
faq.answer: The skill is documentation-only, but its instructions mention a reporter agent and local file writes.

faq.question: Why review permissions before installing?
faq.answer: The source permits writing to ~/.claude, which can affect assistant settings.
